{{nihongo|'''Takatsumi Shrine'''|高積神社}} is a Shinto shrine in Negi, {{ill|Wakayama (city)|Q200747|qid=Q200747}}, Wakayama Prefecture. It is treated as a candidate shrine either for the Meishin-taisha Tsumatsuhime Shrine or for the two small shikinaisha Takatsumihiko and Takatsumihime shrines. Its former modern rank was village shrine. {{nihongo|'''Takatsumi Shrine'''|高積神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Kii Province]].

The shrine has two sites on Mt. Takatsumi (237 m, also called Wasayama): the upper shrine on the summit and the lower shrine at the foot.

* Oyamazumi-no-kami, Ketsuwake-no-kami, Emperor Ojin
* Empress Jingu, Hime-no-Okami

== History ==
The foundation is unknown. One major theory identifies this shrine with "Tsumatsuhime Shrine" (Meishin-taisha) in the Engishiki; another identifies it with "Takatsumihiko" and "Takatsumihime" small shrines. The first record linked to Tsumatsuhime appears in the ''Shoku Nihongi'' (702), mentioning transfer of deities including Itakiso, Ooyatsuhime, and Tsumatsuhime.

The ''Shinsho Gecchokufu-sho'' (806) records endowments to "Tsumatobihime no Kami" in Kii. In the ''Engishiki Jinmyocho'' (927), "Tsumatsuhime Shrine, Meishin-taisha, monthly and niiname offerings" is listed in Nagusa District.

In a medieval water-rights dispute (1433) between Hinokuma/Kunikakasu shrines and Wasa estate, records claimed this shrine had ancient relocations and great authority. The ''Kii Zoku Fudoki'' considered identification with Tsumatsuhime highly plausible.

In 1873 it was ranked village shrine. In 1910, more than ten shrines in the Wasa area, including Keshizume Shrine, were merged into Takatsumi Shrine.

== Divine ranks ==
Records include elevations of deities identified as Tsumatsuhime, Takatsumihiko, and Takatsumihime in classical sources such as the ''Nihon Sandai Jitsuroku'' and ''Kii no Kuni Jinmyocho''.
